name: Pressure and Sealed Casings
description: Smog shut in a sealed casing forces itself up through a filter in the roof.

pages.title: Pressure and Sealed Casings
pages.text:
[#](FFFFFF)[#]() **Key points**

- Smog shut in a sealed space is forced up through the **Filter Frames in its roof**, no pump needed
- The fuller the space, the faster
- **Casing** on a belt, shaft, pipe, door or trapdoor seals a wall (a door only while shut)
- [#](FFFFFF)[#]() Full with nowhere to go, it blows up

Seal a smoky machine inside full blocks, put a Filter Frame in the roof, and its smog finds the way out through the filter.\
\
Sealed means no open side, no gap to the sky, and fewer than 2,048 blocks of room inside.

pages.title: How fast
pages.text:
Each frame in the roof takes smog as fast as it filters: iron 2 units a second, gold 4, diamond 8. A nearly empty space only seeps; a packed one hits that limit.\
\
The frame's top needs a way to the sky, as in any exhaust: open air above it, or a chimney.

pages.title: Belts and gaps
pages.text: Smog leaks through anything without a full face: bare belts, shafts and pipes, fences, carpets, trapdoors. Put Andesite or Brass Casing on a belt where it passes the wall. Items ride through, smog stays in.

pages.title: Shafts and pipes
pages.text:
Case a shaft where it passes the wall with Andesite or Brass Casing, a fluid pipe with Copper Casing. Power and fluid go through, smog stays in.\
\
Gearboxes, chain drives, clutches, gearshifts, encased cogwheels and fans are whole blocks and seal like stone. A shaft in a Metal Girder leaks.

pages.title: Doors and trapdoors
pages.text:
Every door and trapdoor leaks. Right-click any one with Andesite, Brass or Copper Casing to case it.\
\
Shut, a cased door or trapdoor seals like stone. Open, smog gets through as usual.

pages.title: Opening a cased door
pages.text:
Only redstone opens it: a button, lever, pressure plate or circuit. Hands can't, and villagers and mobs can't get through.\
\
A wrench takes the casing off and gives the door back; sneak with the wrench to pick it all up. Breaking it drops both.

pages.title: A sealed smelter
pages.text:
1. Fan, lava (or a Blaze Burner) and belt inside a box of full blocks
2. Casing on the belt, shafts, pipes and door through the wall
3. A Filter Frame in the roof
4. Open sky or a chimney above the frame

Each item smelted sends smog up through the filter.

pages.title: Overpressure
pages.text: [#](FFFFFF)[#]() **Watch out:** a sealed space that fills up has no room for more smoke. A furnace or other machine in it blows up after a few tries and breaks. A fan smelting into it blows the casing open, as hard as a Creeper, after 4 batches that find no room.

pages.title: Reading a filter
pages.text:
Wear **Engineer's Goggles** and look at a Filter Frame. It shows the room under its stack, how full of smog that room is, whether it is filling up or clearing, and how many units a second the stack filters.\
\
Sneak to also see the room's size.

pages.title: Green, yellow, red
pages.text:
- [#](2E8B2E)**Normal**[#](): open air below, or the filters keep up
- [#](B8860B)**Pressure**[#](): sealed room a quarter full, or the stack filtering flat out
- [#](B22222)**Overpressure**[#](): sealed room 60%% full, or its stack's top closed

On red, a smoky machine in the room can blow. Add frames, use better ones, or open the top.
